intro: Our vision, mission, goal and objectives, set down in full.
vision: Chaithanya Kala Bharathi aspires to create a self-reliant, just society where women, children, marginalised tribes, Dalits and other vulnerable sections of the community will lead a sociable life of good understanding, harmony and dignity, without any exploitation, gender bias or other social distortions. CKB believes this would be the result of sustainable development and empowerment.
mission: Socio-economic reconstruction of the target community through rehabilitation of the vulnerable social groups, with a just social action promoting sustainable livelihoods, food security and espousing the alternative life style.
goal: Rural reconstruction and sustainable development of the target community by creating vast avenues, promoting livelihood initiatives and food security in the best possible interest, social justice and empowerment.
objectives: To promote the cultural entity and renovate the existing cultural and traditional practices in the target area, further enriching the sublimity of culture.
To promote the rural entrepreneurship development initiative as a horizon to reconstruct the livelihood system of the rural poor.
To empower the women community for their holistic development, with special priority for the maintenance of gender equity.
To take quality health care to the door steps of the rural community through village animators, preventive and curative care.
To educate the illiterate community as a whole, with special focus on women and children, propagating the noble values of education and establishing residential schools and creches for children.
To provide relief and rehabilitation to the needy in areas affected by natural calamities and emergencies.

To create consensus public awareness on environment, land, forests, water and sanitation, health, HIV/AIDS, women and human rights, the Right to Information Act, the SC/ST Atrocity Act and all other provisions conducive to the betterment of the target community.
To form and promote women's self-help groups and Mahila Mandals, elevating the paths for economic reconstruction and rehabilitation by upgrading their skills and existing potential.
To strengthen the PRI system, bringing out effective leadership qualities and generating demand for village reconstruction.
To provide education and rehabilitation programmes for disabled and blind children.
To provide safe and clean drinking water through bore wells in acute areas, and toilets.

To initiate measures for the establishment of short stay homes for child labourers and orphanages for deserted children, with special provision for vocational and other educational courses for their character building.
To develop models of environmentally sustainable agriculture for food and nutrition security.
To undertake programmes of habitation and rehabilitation, so that the benefits reach the needy poor of the target community.

To promote and provide access to health service delivery in inaccessible areas, creating better health practices among women and adolescent girls, with a special focus on reproductive, women's and child health.
To establish good linkages with the government and voluntary sectors for effective resource mobilisation, promoting networks at all levels.
